title: Climate Change Impact on Pesticide Toxicity in Bumblebees
context: Applied Survival Analysis — Course Research Paper
short_description: Survival analysis of how future heatwave conditions alter pesticide toxicity in bumblebee colonies.
long_description: Modeled bumblebee survival (n = 3,180, across 8 colonies) under current-day vs. future climate-change heatwave scenarios crossed with three pesticide treatments, using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox Proportional Hazards models with colony-level and scenario x pesticide interaction terms. Found that although the future heatwave scenario roughly doubles baseline hazard, its interaction with pesticide exposure significantly reduced pesticide toxicity relative to current conditions — a counterintuitive result possibly explained by heat-triggered colony immune responses such as increased grooming, propolis deployment, and altruistic self-removal of exposed workers.
